finding.message: Sanitizing SVG content string with an incomplete regex filter.
answers: svg_content
svg_content flows into re.sub() replacement logic.
Regular expression fails to strip malformed tags like `</script  >`.
re.sub() sink mechanism outputting sanitized string.
Attacker uploads malicious SVG bypassing filter to trigger Stored XSS.

finding.message: Unsanitized user input is interpolated directly into a SQL string via f-string.
answers: user_input
user_input is concatenated into query string via f-string interpolation.
No parameterized query or escaping is applied before cursor.execute().
cursor.execute() is the sink receiving the tainted SQL string.
Attacker injects SQL payload such as ' OR 1=1-- to manipulate query logic.

finding.message: User-controlled filename is passed to open() without path traversal validation.
answers: filename
filename is joined with base directory via os.path.join() without stripping ../ sequences.
os.path.join does not prevent traversal if filename starts with / or contains ../.
open() is the sink receiving the potentially traversed path.
Attacker supplies ../../etc/passwd to read arbitrary system files.

finding.message: URL parameter from Flask request.args is passed directly to requests.get() without domain validation.
answers: url
url originates from flask.request.args.get('url') — fully user-controlled.
No allowlist or scheme validation is applied to the URL before the HTTP call.
requests.get() is the sink making the outbound HTTP request.
Attacker supplies http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ to access cloud metadata.

finding.message: User-supplied target_ip is interpolated into a shell command string executed with shell=True.
answers: target_ip
target_ip is embedded into a shell command via f-string: f'ping -c 1 {target_ip}'.
No shell metacharacter escaping or input validation is performed.
subprocess.run(..., shell=True) is the sink executing the constructed command.
Attacker supplies '127.0.0.1; rm -rf /' to execute arbitrary OS commands.

finding.message: User-controlled bytes are passed to pickle.loads() without magic byte validation.
answers: session_data
session_data is received as raw bytes from an HTTP cookie without integrity check.
No HMAC signature or magic byte prefix validation is performed before deserialization.
pickle.loads() is the sink deserializing the untrusted bytes.
Attacker crafts a malicious pickle payload to execute arbitrary Python code on the server.

finding.message: Multiple user-controlled parameters flow into render_template_string(), enabling Server-Side Template Injection.
answers: template, username, email
All three parameters originate from user-supplied HTTP form data without sanitization.
Jinja2 evaluates {{ }} and {% %} expressions inside the template string at runtime.
render_template_string() is the sink executing the Jinja2 template with user-controlled context.
Attacker injects {{config}} or {{''.__class__.__mro__}} to leak secrets or achieve RCE.

finding.message: Flask route handler reads raw HTML from request.data and applies an incomplete tag-stripping regex.
answers: flask.request.data
Request body flows into the function via flask.request.data — no explicit parameter.
The tag-stripping regex strips <script> but misses variations like <Script> or <scr\0ipt>.
The filtered HTML string is returned in the HTTP response and rendered in the browser.
Attacker sends crafted request body to inject script tags bypassing the filter.
